dedupe_keys.name: metr la and pems bay traffic forecasting benchmarks dcrnn

description: METR-LA (Los Angeles) and PEMS-BAY (San Francisco Bay Area) are the traffic data files released with the Diffusion Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (DCRNN) paper at ICLR 2018, and have become standard benchmarks for graph-based traffic forecasting. The repository gives metr-la.h5 and pems-bay.h5, each a pandas data frame in HDF5 with one column per sensor and one row per timestamp at 5-minute steps, plus scripts that generate train, validation and test splits, and a TensorFlow implementation of DCRNN. Coverage is two metropolitan road networks. Access: the files are free on Google Drive or Baidu Yun linked from the README; the code is under the MIT licence, and the README states no separate data licence. Caveats: the README does not describe the collection periods or how sensors were chosen, and results tuned to these benchmarks may not transfer to other networks. They support calibration and validation of traffic state models and network flow forecasts. They complement Caltrans PeMS, the Seattle loop detector data set and UTD19 catalogued here.
